title: Ceremonial Helpers (Trivial Standard Wrappers)
pattern: Writing fine-grained helper methods that simply wrap standard library collection operations with no additional validation or logic.
why_bad: It increases the cognitive surface of the codebase by introducing a verbose, custom API for a standard operation that every developer already knows.
detection: Functions whose bodies are exactly one line calling a standard library collection method with raw parameters.
counterexample: Helper functions that perform authorization checks, logging, or complex structural validations prior to insertion.
fix: Inline the helper method directly at all call sites and delete the helper function.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4 ("Modules Should Be Deep - Classitis"), p. 25.
